newsitem.title: USA: EchoStar debt down but News deal still seen.
newsitem.headline: EchoStar debt down but News deal still seen.

text.p: EchoStar Communications Corp debt turned sharply lower on Monday after the company said the planned $1.0 billion investment by News Corp Ltd has been delayed, traders and analysts said.
But high-yield analysts also said the delay should not stand in the way of the deal's completion.
EchoStar's 12-7/8 percent senior secured discount notes due 2004 traded off three points to 83 bid, according to traders. EchoStar's subordinated debt was off about five points at 75 bid, they added.

News Corp on Friday indicated it will not proceed with the investment unless EchoStar abandons its existing system of consumer access to satellite-delivered television programs in favor of a News Corp affiliated system. The delivery of new conditions delayed News Corp's application for regulatory approval beyond the end of April as planned, EchoStar said.

Eric Tutterow, high-yield media and telecommunications analyst at KDP Investment Advisors Inc, said the subject of access control systems has been an open point since the transaction was announced and that an ultimatum from News Corp may be an attempt to get more for its money -- especially since EchoStar stock is now lower than when the deal was announced.
But News Corp's alternatives in the satellites are less attractive and the agreement does not appear to be in jeopardy, Tutterow said.

"You have to look at it from (News Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Rupert) Murdoch's point of view if he walks away from the EchoStar deal -- first of all he'd have to give them $200 million as a loan which would provide EchoStar with all the near-term financing it needs.

Further, EchoStar's position over TCI Satellite Entertainment is a dominant one, Tutterow said. Topping the advantages, EchoStar controls 90 out of 256 licensed frequencies compared with TSAT's 22, he said.
The $200 million loan to EchoStar was negotiated in the initial agreement between the companies.
Another analyst said the access control system may simply be a red herring in place of gamesmanship between Murdoch and EchoStar Chief Executive Officer Charles Ergen.
"You have some exceptionally strong personalities here and for us to expect (a deal) to go 100 percent smoothly would be a bit naive...I am still optimistic a deal would get done."
